title: Possessive pronouns and endings review
focus: Mix the forms and sentence patterns already taught in this pack.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference

exercises.prompt: Write the Finnish owner form meaning “my”.
exercises.explanation: The owner form of minä is minun. This genitive pronoun tells whose thing it is.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive personal owner forms: form or meaning confused

answerDiagnostics.category: Genitive personal owner forms: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use the genitive owner form, not the basic personal pronoun.

exercises.prompt: Write the noun in “my pen”: minun ___. Use kynä (“pen”).
exercises.explanation: kynä + -ni = kynäni. Choose the ending matching minun.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: First- and second-person possessive endings: form or meaning confused

answerDiagnostics.category: First- and second-person possessive endings: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the basic noun and add its possessive ending. The owner pronoun does not replace that ending.

exercises.prompt: Write the noun in “his book”: hänen ___. Use kirja (“book”).
exercises.explanation: kirja + -nsa = kirjansa. Hänen and heidän share the same noun ending; keep the owner pronoun to distinguish the owners.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Shared third-person possessive endings: form or meaning confused

answerDiagnostics.category: Shared third-person possessive endings: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the basic noun and add its possessive ending. The owner pronoun does not replace that ending.

exercises.prompt: Write the noun in “his pillow”: hänen ___. Use tyyny (“pillow”).
exercises.explanation: tyyny takes -nsä: the front vowels ä, ö, y require -nsä when there is no back vowel. The owner pronoun does not decide vowel harmony.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Third-person possessive vowel harmony: form or meaning confused

answerDiagnostics.category: Third-person possessive vowel harmony: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Keep the basic noun and add its possessive ending. The owner pronoun does not replace that ending.

exercises.prompt: Translate “Tämä on minun tyynyni.” into English.
exercises.explanation: Tämä on identifies this singular thing. The owner pronoun and suffix together give its owner.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Simple ownership identity sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: tämä + on + genitive owner pronoun + noun with matching possessive ending

parts.formation: Tämä is the supplied basic singular word for “this”.
Olla uses on because the thing being identified is singular; the owner can still be plural.
Use the learned genitive form: minun. Genitive means the form naming whose thing it is.
tyyny + -ni = tyynyni. The ending marks the owner, not several things.

exercises.prompt: Write “This is your ball.” in Finnish. Use tämä (“this”), on (“is”), and sinun pallosi (“your ball”). The owner pronoun is optional. Address one person.
exercises.explanation: The ending on pallosi already identifies the owner, so both the pronoun-free and explicit-pronoun sentences are natural.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.targetSkill: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: tämä + on + noun with possessive ending

parts.formation: Tämä is the supplied basic singular word for “this”.
Olla uses on because the thing being identified is singular; the owner can still be plural.
pallo + -si = pallosi. The ending marks the owner, not several things.

answerDiagnostics.category: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: In standard written Finnish, omitting the pronoun is possible here; omitting the possessive noun ending is not.

exercises.prompt: Write “Whose ball is this?” in Finnish. Use pallo (“ball”), tämä (“this”), and on (“is”). Put the noun immediately after the question word.
exercises.explanation: Recall kenen for “whose”, then place the basic noun before tämä on. Keep the noun free of a personal possessive ending.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
